text: The spéir-bhean is an Irish heroine. The name comes from the words spear-ban and sky woman. She is a late form of the goddess of Sovereignty. By her right a king could rule in Ireland. The bards of the time painted her as a beautiful young woman, perhaps from the Otherworld. She walked the roads looking for the true leader of the land. Her name appears as Cathleen Ní Houlihan. It is also Róisín Dubh or Dark Rosaleen. Sometimes she is the poor old woman, the Shan Van Vocht, who grows young again when the rightful king kisses her. William Butler Yeats wrote a play for her in his work for the leader Maude Gonne.
